description: T902 context dump - the red/green transcripts of the new isolation regression, the guard-blindness measurement that explains why this incident class had no control, the three plain-git probes behind the mechanism diagnosis, and the 3-run live-clone smoke on both sides of the fix. Companion to findings/T902-private-index.json. claims[]/new_rows[] are empty by contract (a dump is narrative, not a proposal).

    | b.log: git-commit-mine: REFUSED - HEAD holds only 1 files.

Arm 1 of that suite is titled "two concurrent runs, disjoint paths, one commit delayed -> each
commit contains ONLY its own paths". It is the control that would have caught b47c248's shape,
and the guard had it refusing before it could measure anything.
mechanism_probes:
WHY THE MECHANISM DIAGNOSIS IS NOT A GUESS. Three direct probes with plain git, no wrapper:

  probe 1 - pathspec vs index commit
    A stages a.txt; B stages b.txt; B runs `git commit -m msg -- b.txt`
      -> commit contains b.txt; a.txt STILL STAGED afterwards.
    B then runs plain `git commit`
      -> commit contains a.txt.
    So capture requires COMMIT_MODE=index, and the wrapper's paths-mode is already safe.

  probe 2 - private index, foreign staging present
    A stages a.txt in .git/index; B does
      GIT_INDEX_FILE=$P git read-tree HEAD; GIT_INDEX_FILE=$P git add -f -- b.txt;
      GIT_INDEX_FILE=$P git commit -m "B private"
      -> commit contains b.txt alone; `git diff --cached` still shows a.txt.
    Isolation confirmed at the git level before any wrapper code was written.

  probe 3 - the reconcile is necessary, not defensive
    Immediately after probe 2, `git status --short` read `MM b.txt`: the shared index still held
    b.txt at its pre-commit blob, so the file read as staged-for-reversion against the new HEAD.
    `git reset -q -- b.txt` cleared it. That is why the wrapper reconciles, and why arm 4 asserts
    both `git diff --cached` and `git status --porcelain -uno` are empty.
live_smoke:
LIVE-CLONE SMOKE, 3 runs each side.
Setup per run: `git clone --no-hardlinks` of the live repo (root commit
ef58d0f45fd453fc850b9638d5527354c40f9f6f, 2741 files at HEAD, so the T771 size guard is ACTIVE),
core.hooksPath=tools/hooks with the real hook, live bin/ copied in, working-tree versions of
tools/git-commit-mine + tools/git-commit-mine-lib.sh + tools/hooks/pre-commit installed (the fix
is uncommitted, so a plain clone would have measured HEAD's wrapper - the first attempt did
exactly that and had to be discarded). Two real bundles with real deliverables=, two concurrent
wrapper invocations, and a third console's bare `git add -- docs/INDEX.md` staged throughout.

AFTER the fix:
  run 1: clone root=ef58d0f...  files at HEAD=2741
    A rc=0 commit=27b8e2a files: [docs/status/CURRENT.md ]
    B rc=0 commit=d8a59b5 files: [docs/status/HANDOVER.md ]
    console C's bare-staged docs/INDEX.md still staged? [docs/INDEX.md ]
    shared index vs HEAD clean (tracked)? [M  docs/INDEX.md  M tools/git-commit-mine  M tools/hooks/pre-commit ]
  run 2: A rc=0 commit=93bbd36 files: [docs/status/CURRENT.md ]
         B rc=0 commit=de6549d files: [docs/status/HANDOVER.md ]
         console C's docs/INDEX.md still staged
  run 3: A rc=0 commit=6d43a9e files: [docs/status/CURRENT.md ]
         B rc=0 commit=0d7318f files: [docs/status/HANDOVER.md ]
         console C's docs/INDEX.md still staged
  hook, both consoles, all runs:
    pre-commit: unlabelled commit, no staged path held by any live row - allowed
    pre-commit: claimlint ... - <= floor, allowed - test gate: bypassed with recorded reason
  (The two `M tools/...` entries are the installed fix itself, deliberately left uncommitted in
   the clone. docs/INDEX.md is console C's work, still staged, still unattributed to A or B.)

BEFORE the fix, identical setup, pre-fix wrapper + pre-fix hook:
  run 1: A rc=1 commit= files: []
         B rc=1 commit= files: []
         console C's bare-staged docs/INDEX.md still staged? [docs/INDEX.md docs/status/CURRENT.md docs/status/HANDOVER.md ]
         shared index vs HEAD clean (tracked)? [M  docs/INDEX.md A  docs/status/CURRENT.md M  docs/status/HANDOVER.md ]
  run 2: identical.  run 3: identical.
  A's log: git-commit-mine: REFUSED - index contains staged paths outside your scope
             (bundle untracked/SMOKE-A.md): docs/INDEX.md, docs/status/HANDOVER.md
  B's log: git-commit-mine: REFUSED - index contains staged paths outside your scope
             (bundle untracked/SMOKE-B.md): docs/INDEX.md

  Read the pre-fix "still staged" line again: docs/status/CURRENT.md and docs/status/HANDOVER.md
  are in it. Neither console committed anything, and BOTH left their own paths staged in the
  shared index on their way out, because the pre-fix wrapper stages before it verifies. The
  guard against sweeping was seeding the next sweep. 0 of 6 commits landed across 3 runs; each
  run left two more consoles' paths sitting in shared state.

  Note also what the pre-fix reds show and do NOT show: two real wrapper invocations BLOCK each
  other rather than capturing, because both have scope and both refuse. Capture needs a
  committer that does not consult the index - the plain `git commit` of arm 1. Blockage and
  capture are the same defect seen from two sides; only blockage ever looked like an error.
notes: The three null arms (4,5,6) PASS on both the pre-fix and post-fix wrapper. That is the point of them: without a green null control on the pre-fix code, the three reds could have been the harness failing rather than the wrapper. Arm 4 in particular is the control for the fix's own side effect - it fails if the shared-index reconcile is ever dropped, which is a defect the fix INTRODUCES and must therefore carry a check for.
